profiles.name: Linux: temporarily stop creation of new MPTCP sockets
profiles.control: kernel feature switch (per network namespace)
profiles.when_to_use: Only if a Linux system may be affected, the relevant vendor kernel fix is not active, and MPTCP disruption is acceptable.
before: Back up configuration and arrange service maintenance.
Identify all relevant network namespaces and MPTCP-using services.
Plan to restart affected MPTCP listeners; existing sockets may remain.
steps: Read the status without changing anything: python3 scripts/mptcp_guard.py status
If it reports available and enabled, inspect running services and approve the outage.
On the Linux host, run: sudo python3 scripts/mptcp_guard.py apply --accept-service-disruption
If services use separate network namespaces, have the administrator assess them individually. This helper manages only its current namespace.
Restart affected listeners during maintenance; inspect normal service traffic.
check: Run: python3 scripts/mptcp_guard.py status; expect knob value 0 in that namespace.
Confirm affected services remain functional without MPTCP; test ordinary IPv4 TCP connections.
Record date, namespace, running kernel and service status. Do NOT call the CVE fixed.
undo: After installing and rebooting into a vendor-fixed kernel, verify the exact running kernel vendor advisory.
If the original boot still has the guard state: sudo python3 scripts/mptcp_guard.py rollback --accept-reexposure
If reboot cleared the runtime guard, inspect current MPTCP setting and restore normal service configuration per vendor guidance.
Verify MPTCP-required applications, plus ordinary connections; close temporary exception ticket.
profiles.limitations: Only restricts creation of new MPTCP sockets in the current network namespace. Existing sockets, other namespaces and non-MPTCP attack paths remain outside its proof. Changes are runtime-only and lost on reboot. Applying and rolling back can interrupt services.

profiles.name: Windows: reduce exposure of an HTTP.sys HTTP/3 endpoint
profiles.control: operator-reviewed protocol exposure reduction
profiles.when_to_use: Only for a vulnerable Windows HTTP.sys server exposing HTTP/3 that cannot yet take Microsoft's update. Requires server administrator.
before: Confirm HTTP.sys hosts HTTP/3; do not confuse browser HTTP/3 with the Windows HTTP.sys server.
Back up current HTTP.sys application and registry configuration. Arrange a maintenance window.
steps: Ask the server administrator to disable HTTP.sys HTTP/3 using their approved Microsoft-documented configuration, or restrict UDP/443 at the perimeter to trusted networks.
Do not assume a local Windows Firewall block works for every HTTP.sys QUIC listener.
Restart the affected service under the change plan; do not automatically restart the shared HTTP service.
check: From an authorized test client, confirm the service does not accept HTTP/3 on the restricted endpoint.
Confirm the normal HTTPS/TCP application path continues working and inspect service logs.
Record the effective network policy and HTTP.sys configuration; no CVE-fixed claim.
undo: Install Microsoft's signed update for the exact Windows edition and build, restart, verify active build and normal service function.
Restore the previous HTTP/3 policy/configuration in the approved maintenance window.
Test HTTP/3 and HTTPS/TCP with authorized clients.
profiles.limitations: Network rules can have exceptions or interception differences. Microsoft HTTP.sys is distinct from other QUIC stacks. This is administrator-assisted containment only.

profiles.name: Chrome: limit exposure until the official browser update is active
profiles.control: browser settings and optional isolation
profiles.when_to_use: Google Chrome Stable cannot be updated promptly; do not assume the settings defeat the multi-bug exploit chain.
before: Do not open unknown sites or attachments in a known-affected browser.

steps: On a computer, open Chrome → Settings → Privacy and security → Security → Manage JavaScript optimization & security.
Select 'Don't allow sites to use JavaScript optimization' when available; the option may affect site performance or function.

check: Reopen the settings page to confirm the setting is still selected.
Open a trusted page and check required actions; do not test an exploit.
undo: Use Chrome → Settings → About Chrome to install Google's signed stable update; relaunch.
Recheck the active full Chrome version and run the catalog version checker for each listed CVE.
Return settings to the site's approved baseline only after confirming the vendor update and acceptable risk.
profiles.limitations: V8 optimizer control is not established as a workaround for all Chrome chains or every CVE. It may not protect other vulnerabilities.

profiles.control: signed upstream/vendor fixes and conditional decompression restriction

before: Inventory native linked Brotli and all container, dependency, runtime and OEM layers. Confirm that untrusted input reaches the decoder; mere package presence is not proof of exploitability.

steps: Use corresponding upstream Brotli fixed version 1.0.10, 1.1.1, or 1.2.1 where applicable; rebuild and redeploy binaries, not just update package manifests.

For .NET use Microsoft's fixed serviced runtimes (8.0.33, 9.0.22, 10.0.14), when applicable; test restarted application workloads.
For Siemens industrial products follow the exact Siemens ProductCERT device/product advice; a generic Brotli library hotfix is not a signed industrial controller update.

If an approved upgrade is unavailable, consider refusing untrusted Brotli decoding in the affected app, with explicit functional testing. Blocking incoming Content-Encoding: br alone does not cover other Brotli inputs.
check: Verify exact loaded runtime/native library or static-binary revision after restarting and re-deploying; confirm vendor backports via written bulletin.
Test legitimate compression paths, business applications and independent incident monitoring without transmitting hostile payloads.
undo: Roll back ingress decompression restrictions only after a fixed runtime and normal service tests are confirmed.
Never downgrade to affected decoder code; use vendor-supported recovery for failed deployments.
profiles.limitations: Cross-language CVE; version floors in this repository apply only to upstream Brotli decoder library releases, not to bundled products/OS packages. Untrusted decompression is the exposure path. No universal binary patch or full network-only mitigation.
